answer: The attacker pays in compute, time, and reputation every time an alias is slashed, and these costs grow faster than the influence the cluster gains, making a large coordinated farm economically self-defeating. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a dawn as the anchor of the cost. A echo stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a bridge...
